zh.summary: 從虛構簡訊與來電案例，分辨語音釣魚、簡訊釣魚與身分冒充，練習獨立查證、驗證碼防護與證據判讀。

sourceBody.text: CEH M09-03｜語音釣魚、簡訊釣魚與身分冒充
Module 09：Social Engineering（社交工程） 本課主題：Vishing、Smishing、Impersonation
今天接著 M09-02 的 Phishing（釣魚：利用欺騙性訊息，誘導人交出資訊或採取不安全行動） 往下學。上一課主要問「攻擊者鎖定誰」；這一課改問：對方透過什麼管道接近你，又憑什麼讓你相信他的身分？
不用先懂電話系統或網路設定。本課會從生活情境，一步步連到身分驗證、驗證碼、防護與證據判讀。可以分段讀，不需要為了跟上排程一次讀完。
一、先想像：簡訊與電話互相證明，就一定可信嗎？
以下 Northstar 教材中心、人物與事件都是虛構案例，只用來練習判斷，沒有對任何真實對象發送訊息或測試。
小林正在整理課程資料，手機收到一則簡訊，大意是：「教材平台出現異常登入，請聯絡服務人員處理。」
不久後電話響了。對方自稱平台客服，說得出小林的名字與教材專案名稱，來電畫面也顯示熟悉的服務名稱。對方表示要「協助取消異常操作」，請小林把剛收到的登入驗證碼念出來。
小林可能會想：
簡訊先提醒，客服又打來，而且知道我的工作，應該是真的吧？
但從資安角度看，我們目前只知道「收到一則簡訊」和「有人來電」。如果兩個管道都由同一個攻擊者安排，它們只是互相配合的說法，不是兩份獨立證明。
本課最重要的一句話是：
看起來像、聽起來像、知道你的事，都不等於身分已驗證；身分驗證通過，也不等於每項要求都有授權。
二、三個名詞：兩個在說管道，一個在說冒充手法
1. Vishing：語音釣魚
Vishing 是 Voice phishing（利用語音的釣魚） 的組合詞。有人透過電話、語音通話或語音留言，以欺騙方式誘導你交出資料或採取不安全的行動，就屬於這個範圍。
例如，有人冒充資訊人員，要求你提供登入資訊。重點是利用語音互動取得信任，不是「有電話」就算攻擊，也不要求一定使用假聲音。真人正常說話，也可能進行語音釣魚。[加拿大資安中心：語音釣魚](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/what-voice-phishing-vishing-itsap00102)
它可以要求的，不只密碼，還可能包括同意帳號操作、付款、提供文件，或允許遠端協助。正常客服也會打電話，所以分類要同時看欺騙、目的與要求，不能只看通訊工具。
2. Smishing：簡訊釣魚
Smishing 結合了 SMS（Short Message Service，手機簡訊服務） 與 phishing。典型做法是以欺騙性簡訊，誘導收件者交出敏感資料、進入假網站或執行其他危險動作。
例如假借配送、帳務或登入異常，要求從簡訊內的入口處理。簡訊可以帶連結，也可能只要求回覆資料或撥打電話；「沒有連結」不等於安全。[加拿大資安中心：簡訊釣魚](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/guidance/smishing-protect-yourself-sms-attacks-itsap00103)
本課先用「SMS 簡訊」掌握這個詞。通訊軟體裡也可能有釣魚與冒充，但不是看到任何文字訊息，都要不分管道地叫作 Smishing。
3. Impersonation：身分冒充
Impersonation 指假扮成其他人、角色或組織，讓你把原本給那個身分的信任交給冒充者。
例如假冒客服、主管、同事或來訪廠商。它描述的是「扮成誰」，不是限定某個管道：電話、簡訊、電子郵件、通訊軟體，甚至面對面都可能發生。官方社交工程指引也將假冒可信人物列為常見手法。[加拿大資安中心：社交工程](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/guidance/social-engineering-itsap00166)
把三個詞排在一起，就比較不會背錯：

rows: Vishing 語音釣魚
透過什麼管道誘導？
用電話要求提供登入驗證碼
Smishing 簡訊釣魚
透過什麼管道誘導？
用欺騙性簡訊引導處理假事件
Impersonation 身分冒充
假扮成誰來取得信任？
自稱教材平台客服

sourceBody.text: 這不是三選一的互斥分類。 一次事件可以先有簡訊釣魚，再有語音釣魚，而且兩段都使用身分冒充。釣魚跨管道進行的現象，也見於 NIST（美國國家標準暨技術研究院）的說明。[NIST：釣魚管道與防護](https://www.nist.gov/blogs/cybersecurity-insights/phishing-resistance-protecting-keys-your-kingdom)
三、接回上一課：目標、管道、身分，是不同觀察角度
M09-02 的 Spear phishing（魚叉式釣魚／定向釣魚），重點是針對特定對象設計；Whaling（鯨釣），重點是鎖定高階、高價值人物。
今天的 Vishing 與 Smishing，重點則是管道。
因此，在小林的案例，如果查證後確認對方特別蒐集他的工作背景、量身設計內容，可以描述為「針對小林的定向釣魚，透過簡訊與語音接觸，並冒充平台客服」。這比硬選一個名詞更完整。
反過來，對方聲稱「我是董事長」，也不代表事件自動變成鯨釣。仍要分清楚：

items: 鎖定誰：希望哪個人照做？
透過哪裡：電話、簡訊或其他管道？
冒充誰：借用哪個身分？
要求什麼：資料、登入、付款、權限或其他行動？

sourceBody.text: 這四個問題是本課整理的判讀工具，不是官方規定的攻擊階段。
四、為什麼來電顯示、聲音與個人資料都不夠？
1. 來電顯示是畫面線索，不是完整的身分證明
Caller ID（來電顯示） 是手機畫面上顯示的來電號碼或名稱。Spoofing（偽冒） 則是讓某項識別資訊看起來像來自別的來源；本課特別指偽冒來電顯示。
來電顯示可以被操弄，所以「畫面上是銀行或公司的號碼」，不能單獨證明電話另一端就是該機構。[美國聯邦貿易委員會：辨認詐騙](https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-avoid-scam)
這裡再分清楚兩個詞：

items: 身分冒充：整體上假扮成客服或主管。
來電顯示偽冒：操弄畫面上的號碼或名稱，是可能使用的其中一項技術。

sourceBody.text: 對方即使使用普通陌生號碼，也能在說話時冒充客服。因此，身分冒充不一定需要來電顯示偽冒。
2. 聲音很像，也只能增加熟悉感
AI（Artificial Intelligence，人工智慧）語音複製，是用技術產生近似某人的聲音。官方消費者防詐資料已提醒，熟悉的聲音也可能被模仿。[FTC：語音複製與緊急求助詐騙](https://consumer.ftc.gov/consumer-alerts/2023/03/scammers-use-ai-enhance-their-family-emergency-schemes)
不過，我們不能反過來說「聲音怪怪的，所以一定是 AI 攻擊」；通訊品質也可能造成失真。正常、流暢的聲音，同樣不能保證安全。
防守目標不是靠耳朵猜出所有假聲音，而是讓重要操作不只依賴聲音。
3. 知道你的背景，不等於有權要求你操作
小林的名字、專案名稱可能出現在公開網站，也可能來自其他來源。單靠電話裡說得出這些內容，無法判定資訊來源，更無法證明對方的身分與權限。
這是推理上的界線：知道某項資料，與有資格替這個帳號做決定，是兩件事。 不需要先證明背景資料從哪裡外洩，才願意暫停可疑要求。
五、真正要守住的是哪一道界線？
回到小林的電話，對方要的不是「聊幾句」，而是讓小林交出一個可以協助完成帳號操作的驗證碼。
Authentication（身分驗證） 是確認正在使用服務的人是否掌握該身分所需的驗證條件。Authorization（授權） 是決定這個人可以執行哪些操作。
生活類比：櫃檯確認你是公司員工，不代表你就能領走公司的全部鑰匙。
同樣地，就算確認電話另一端確實是某位同事，還是要確認：這項資料可以給他嗎？他有權批准付款嗎？是否走完必要流程？
登入驗證碼為什麼不能當成客服的身分證？
OTP（One-Time Password，一次性密碼／驗證碼） 通常只在有限條件下有效，用來協助驗證某次操作。它可能真的來自平台，卻不代表「叫你把碼念出來的人」也是真的客服。
用本課的虛構情境理解：如果有人在別處嘗試登入，平台可能把真正的驗證碼送給帳號持有人。持有人再受騙把碼交出去，就可能讓別人完成那次驗證。這是風險示意，不是已發生的事實；實際是否成功仍要查紀錄。
MFA（Multi-Factor Authentication，多因素驗證） 是使用不同類型的驗證因素，例如密碼搭配你持有的驗證裝置。它能增加保護，但不是所有 MFA 都具有同樣的抗釣魚能力。
NIST 明確區分：需要使用者手動輸入的 OTP 等驗證輸出，不應視為具備抗釣魚能力，因為這個輸出沒有綁定到正在驗證的特定連線工作階段（一段特定的驗證互動），可能被轉交到真正服務。[NIST SP 800-63B-4：抗釣魚能力](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html#phishres)
現在先記住：

items: 自己從可信入口發起操作，與應陌生來電要求提供登入驗證碼，不是同一件事。
不提供登入驗證碼、密碼或復原碼給未驗證的來電者。
不因對方說「為了資安」，就關閉保護或核准自己沒發起的驗證要求。
抗釣魚驗證主要保護登入驗證環節，不能替你判斷每筆付款或資料交付是否合理。M09-06 會再深入整套防護。

sourceBody.text: 六、完整拆解 Northstar 案例：先辨認風險，再查證
下面是本課合成情境的分析，不是實際事件調查結果。

rows: 簡訊叫小林從新入口處理登入異常
把處理入口交由未驗證訊息決定
自己開啟原先使用的官方入口
來電自稱客服，知道專案名稱
把熟悉背景當成身分證明
透過既有可信聯絡資料核實
要求念出登入驗證碼
把驗證能力交給未驗證對象
停止提供，交由正式窗口處理
要求保持通話、不要聯絡公司窗口
阻止獨立查證
結束可疑互動，依既有程序確認

sourceBody.text: 「很急」不一定代表詐騙；真的事故也可能很急。但急迫不應成為略過驗證的理由。真正可用的緊急程序，應預先定義由誰確認、誰核准、如何留下紀錄，而不是由電話中的人臨時決定全部規則。
七、如何驗證才算真的離開對方安排的圈子？
Independent verification（獨立查證） 的核心，是改用不由這次可疑要求提供、控制或指定的可信來源，確認身分與要求。
重點不只是「換一個通訊軟體」。如果從可疑簡訊點進客服聊天室，再照聊天室提供的號碼打電話，三個地方可能仍由同一方控制。
在 Northstar 的案例，小林可以這樣做：

items: 1. 停下來：先不提供資料、不核准登入、不安裝軟體。
2. 離開可疑互動：結束電話，不使用來電畫面的一鍵回撥，也不使用簡訊提供的聯絡方式。
3. 自己找到既有入口：例如公司原本的資訊服務台、既存通訊錄或先前確認的官方平台。
4. 核對具體事項：有沒有這張服務工單？誰提出？要做哪項操作？授權範圍是什麼？
5. 依核准流程處理：確認為真，也只做工作需要且已授權的部分；確認不清楚，就交由負責窗口升級處理。

sourceBody.text: 「服務工單」就是一份有編號、內容與處理人的工作紀錄。但對方念得出工單號碼，也不等於工單真的存在或內容正確；要從自己取得的可信入口核對。
這個流程是教學案例的防守設計。官方指引同樣建議使用已知可信電話或正式網站查證，而非使用對方提供的號碼或直接回撥。[加拿大資安中心：來電查證建議](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/what-voice-phishing-vishing-itsap00102)
若懷疑原本可信的帳號也被冒用，僅向同一個帳號再問一次仍不夠。高風險事項應依組織程序，使用另一個已核實的窗口或獨立核准，避免整個決策只依賴單一可能失陷的管道。
八、組織不能只要求員工「自己小心」
接回 M01-06 的 Defense in depth（縱深防禦）：把不同層的控制一起安排，避免一次判斷失誤就造成全部損失。
以下是為 Northstar 設計的控制例子，不表示每間公司都已有這些設定：

rows: 人員與流程
固定查證窗口；允許暫停可疑要求；提供簡單通報方式
讓員工有可執行的下一步，而不只靠辨認口音
帳號
適合系統的抗釣魚驗證；敏感操作重新確認
強化驗證，不代表所有商業要求都可信
權限
只給工作需要的權限；重要變更由不同人確認
減少單一帳號或單一決策能造成的影響
裝置
軟體安裝與遠端協助採正式核准
避免假客服把「協助」變成未授權控制
偵測與應變
保留登入、權限變更、服務工單紀錄；建立通報與處置程序
協助發現及追查，紀錄本身仍可能不完整

sourceBody.text: 正常的遠端協助工具不必然是惡意程式；風險在於誰控制、是否經過驗證與授權、允許做到什麼程度。
這也串起前面的 M01：

items: M01-01：CIA 安全目標。機密性關心資料是否被未授權讀取；完整性關心資料或設定是否被不當修改；可用性關心有權使用的人是否能正常使用。
M01-02：資產與風險。帳號、教材、付款與服務都是要保護的對象；風險要看可能性與後果，不只看訊息有多可疑。
M01-03：授權邊界。教材只分析虛構事件；實際電話演練、蒐證與測試，需要明確範圍和授權。
M01-04／05：入口與行為。電話、簡訊、帳號復原流程都可能成為接觸點；再依實際行為分析，不因一個警訊就宣稱已完成整條攻擊。
M01-07：事件應變。先控制風險，再根據紀錄釐清影響、恢復與改善。

sourceBody.text: 九、證據判讀：接到電話、交出碼、帳號被用，是不同層次
小林事後說：「我有接電話，而且好像念過一組碼。」資安人員應先接住通報，記錄他做過什麼，不責怪，也不直接寫成「全公司資料已外洩」。
下面是教學用證據矩陣：

rows: 手機顯示一則簡訊與一通來電
有相應訊息或通話紀錄
顯示的來源就是真實身分
小林表示自己念出登入驗證碼
有憑證暴露的陳述，應立即依風險處置
對方一定成功登入
平台記錄某次驗證成功
該次驗證流程成功
一定是攻擊者，也不代表讀過全部資料
有不尋常的權限變更或檔案下載
存在需要核查的活動
所有變更都惡意、所有下載都已外傳
獨立窗口確認未曾提出該要求
支持該身分／要求可能遭冒用
事件的全部來源與影響已釐清

sourceBody.text: 要交叉核對的內容可以包括時間、帳號、裝置、實際操作、服務工單及資料存取紀錄。Log（日誌／系統紀錄） 是系統留下的活動記載；它是證據來源之一，不是永遠完整的現場錄影。
找不到異常紀錄，不等於保證沒事；可能是沒有記錄、保存時間不足，或尚未找到正確資料。另一方面，陌生裝置或異常時間也可能有合理原因，仍需查證。
處置不必等到百分之百確定；結論卻要寫在證據能支持的範圍內。 如果已提供密碼、登入驗證碼，或允許可疑遠端協助，應立即透過正式管道通報，由負責人依情況保護帳號、處理工作階段與裝置。不要為了確認而再次執行可疑內容，也不要自行清除所有紀錄。
十、兩分鐘桌上練習：不打電話，也能看見信任從哪裡來
這是紙上觀察，不需要上網、不需要輸入帳號，也不算已完成實作。
在紙上畫兩條路：

visual.caption: 兩條查證路線
visual.description: 每一步的聯絡資料，是誰提供的？

items.title: 路線 A：來源仍在同一圈
items.body: 路線 A：可疑簡訊 → 簡訊內客服連結 → 客服提供的回撥號碼 → 對方說「確實是我們」。

items.title: 路線 B：回到既有可信程序
items.body: 路線 B：可疑簡訊 → 暫停 → 自己開啟既有公司服務台 → 核對工單與承辦人 → 按權限處理。

sourceBody.downloadLabel: 下載查證路線 SVG 圖

sourceBody.text: 把每一步的「聯絡資料是誰提供的」圈出來。
路線 A 看起來查了三次，但查證來源仍由可疑訊息一路提供；路線 B 則把確認權交回原先已建立的可信程序。這是兩者真正的差別，不是用了幾個 App，也不是問了幾次「你真的是客服嗎」。
十一、考試與實務最容易混淆的地方

rows: 電話詐騙一定要用 AI 假聲音
真人、錄音或其他語音形式都可能；AI 不是必要條件
Vishing、Smishing、冒充只能選一個
管道與手法可以同時成立，先看題目問哪個角度
簡訊在熟悉的對話串裡，就是真的
顯示名稱、號碼與對話串位置都不能單獨取代驗證
沒有點連結，所以沒有任何風險
也可能直接提供資料、念出驗證碼或照電話指示操作
換成電話確認，就算獨立查證
要看號碼的來源；用可疑訊息提供的號碼，仍可能落在同一圈
有 MFA 就絕對不會被釣魚
驗證方式不同，保護不同；登入安全也不等於付款授權合理
接到詐騙電話就代表已被入侵
接觸、暴露、登入、操作與損害需要分開查證

sourceBody.text: 其中，假訊息可能混入原本可信簡訊對話串的情況，已有官方防護資料說明；並不是所有手機或所有事件都一定如此。[加拿大資安中心：簡訊來源偽冒](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/guidance/smishing-protect-yourself-sms-attacks-itsap00103)
十二、一個小檢核：請用自己的話判斷
情境： Northstar 的一般行政承辦人收到「帳號需驗證」簡訊，接著有人打電話自稱資訊服務台，正確說出專案名稱。對方要求提供登入驗證碼，並說只能用簡訊裡的號碼回撥確認。承辦人表示已念出驗證碼，目前尚未取得平台登入與資料存取紀錄。
請用幾句話回答同一個情境：

items: 1. 若確認這是攻擊，簡訊、電話與「自稱資訊服務台」各對應本課哪個概念？它們能同時成立嗎？
2. 你會怎麼查證，才能離開對方安排的管道？
3. 現在能直接認定帳號已遭入侵、教材已外洩嗎？請區分已知風險、待查證結果與應先做的事。

sourceBody.text: 不需要寫很多，也不用給信心分數。請先自行作答，再展開下方參考解答比對推理；閱讀解答不等於已完成本人作答或理解驗收。

sourceBody.summary: 參考解答：1. 這三個概念能同時成立嗎？
paragraphs: 可以。若已確認為欺騙性攻擊，SMS 簡訊對應 Smishing（簡訊釣魚），電話中的誘導對應 Vishing（語音釣魚），自稱資訊服務台則是 Impersonation（身分冒充）。
前兩個主要在描述管道，第三個在描述假扮的身分，因此不是互斥分類。知道專案名稱，只能顯示對方掌握該資訊，不能單靠這點證明他是真正的資訊人員。若有證據顯示特別針對該承辦人設計內容，還可從「目標」角度描述為定向釣魚；但題目本身不需要靠猜測補出蒐集過程。

sourceBody.summary: 參考解答：2. 怎麼查證才不留在對方安排的圈子？
paragraphs: 先停止提供資料、核准登入或安裝軟體，結束可疑通話。不要照對方指定的簡訊號碼回撥，也不要把來電顯示當成可信通訊錄。
應從自己原先使用的公司服務台、既有通訊錄或已核實的官方入口，確認有沒有這項要求、工單與承辦人，以及操作範圍和必要核准。來源獨立，比「改用電話或另一個 App」更重要。確認身分後，仍需確認這項操作有授權。

sourceBody.summary: 參考解答：3. 現在能認定帳號遭入侵、教材外洩嗎？
paragraphs: 還不能，但應立即採取風險相稱的保護措施。
目前已有的是收到訊息、接到電話，以及承辦人表示自己提供過登入驗證碼。這是可能的驗證資訊暴露，應立即透過正式管道通報；不需要等到損失證實才處理。
仍待查的是：驗證碼對應什麼操作、是否仍有效、是否完成登入或其他驗證、操作人是否獲授權、進一步做過哪些動作，以及是否有資料遭未授權存取或外傳。需要交叉核對時間、驗證及登入紀錄、帳號和權限變更、裝置、工單與資料活動。
負責窗口可依組織程序，評估保護帳號、撤銷可疑工作階段或處理裝置等措施。不要為了測試再次提供碼或重開可疑內容，也不要自行清除所有證據。
一句話總結：已知風險要及時處置；成功入侵與資料外洩要各自取得證據。
判讀依據
[加拿大資安中心：Vishing](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/what-voice-phishing-vishing-itsap00102)
[加拿大資安中心：Smishing](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/guidance/smishing-protect-yourself-sms-attacks-itsap00103)
[NIST SP 800-63B-4：Phishing resistance](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html#phishres)
上述答案把官方術語與本課虛構案例的推理分開；沒有宣稱案例是真實事件。

sourceBody.text: 本課總結

items: Vishing 看語音管道，Smishing 看簡訊管道，Impersonation 看冒充身分。
熟悉的號碼、聲音、背景與真驗證碼，都不能單獨證明對方及要求可信。
查證要離開可疑來源控制的管道；處置可以先做，結論要依證據。

en.summary: Distinguish vishing, smishing and impersonation through a fictional text-and-call scenario, then practice independent verification, login-code protection and evidence-based reasoning.

sourceBody.text: CEH M09-03 | Vishing, Smishing, and Impersonation
Module 09: Social Engineering Topic: Voice phishing, SMS phishing, and impersonation

This lesson continues M09-02's discussion of phishing: deceptive communications that persuade people to disclose information or take unsafe actions. The previous lesson primarily asked, “Who is being targeted?” This lesson asks, “Which channel is being used, and what makes the claimed identity believable?”

No knowledge of telephone systems or network configuration is required. We will start with an everyday situation and connect it to authentication, verification codes, controls, and evidence. Read in sections if helpful; there is no need to finish everything merely to keep pace with a schedule.
1. If a text and a phone call confirm each other, are they trustworthy?
Northstar Learning Center, the people, and the events below are fictional. They are used only for reasoning practice. No messages were sent to real targets and no real systems were tested.
Lin is preparing course materials when a text arrives. It claims that the learning platform has detected an unusual login and asks him to contact support.

Shortly afterward, someone calls and claims to be platform support. The caller knows Lin's name and the course-material project. The phone display also shows a familiar service name. The caller offers to “cancel the unusual activity” and asks Lin to read out the login verification code he has just received.
Lin might think:
First the text warned me, then support called. They even know my work. Surely this is genuine?
From a security perspective, we currently know only that a text arrived and someone called. If one attacker arranged both channels, they are coordinated claims, not two independent confirmations.
The key idea for this lesson is:
Looking familiar, sounding familiar, or knowing your circumstances does not establish identity. Even a verified identity does not authorize every request.
2. Three terms: two describe channels; one describes pretending to be someone else
Vishing: voice phishing
Vishing combines voice and phishing. It involves deceptive calls, voice conversations, or voice messages that try to make a person disclose information or take unsafe action.

For example, someone poses as IT staff and requests login information. The key is using voice interaction to gain trust. A telephone call alone is not an attack, and a fabricated voice is not required. A real person speaking normally can conduct vishing. [Canadian Centre for Cyber Security: Vishing](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/what-voice-phishing-vishing-itsap00102)

The requested action might involve a password, account approval, payment, documents, or remote assistance. Legitimate support teams also make calls, so assess the deception, purpose, and requested action—not just the tool.
Smishing: SMS phishing

Smishing combines SMS (Short Message Service, mobile text messaging) with phishing. A deceptive text attempts to obtain sensitive information, lead someone to a fake website, or induce another unsafe action.

A message might claim there is a delivery, billing, or login problem and direct the recipient to a new destination. A text can contain a link, but it can also request a reply or a phone call. No link does not mean no risk. [Canadian Centre for Cyber Security: Smishing](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/guidance/smishing-protect-yourself-sms-attacks-itsap00103)

Use SMS as the basic channel associated with this term. Messaging apps can also carry phishing and impersonation, but do not automatically label every written message as smishing without considering its channel.
Impersonation: pretending to be another identity
Impersonation means posing as another person, role, or organization to borrow the trust associated with that identity.

Examples include pretending to be support staff, a manager, a colleague, or a visiting supplier. It describes who the attacker pretends to be, not a particular channel. It can occur by phone, SMS, email, messaging app, or in person. Official social-engineering guidance identifies impersonation of trusted people as a common technique. [Canadian Centre for Cyber Security: Social engineering](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/guidance/social-engineering-itsap00166)
Putting the three terms side by side makes the distinction easier to remember:

rows: Vishing
Which channel is used to induce action?
A phone call requesting a login code
Smishing
Which channel is used to induce action?
A deceptive SMS about a fabricated incident
Impersonation
Which identity is used to gain trust?
Claiming to be platform support

sourceBody.text: These are not mutually exclusive choices. One incident can begin with smishing, continue with vishing, and involve impersonation throughout. NIST, the US National Institute of Standards and Technology, also describes phishing across communication channels. [NIST: Phishing channels and defenses](https://www.nist.gov/blogs/cybersecurity-insights/phishing-resistance-protecting-keys-your-kingdom)
3. Connect to the previous lesson: target, channel, and identity are different dimensions
In M09-02, spear phishing described content tailored to particular targets, while whaling described targeting senior, high-value people.
Vishing and smishing primarily describe the communication channel.

If investigation confirms that someone gathered Lin's work details and tailored the approach, we could describe the case as “targeted phishing against Lin, using SMS and voice while impersonating platform support.” That is more informative than forcing the event into only one category.
Likewise, someone saying “I am the company president” does not automatically make an incident whaling. Separate these questions:

items: Who is targeted? Who is supposed to act?
Which channel is used? Voice, SMS, or something else?
Who is impersonated? Which identity lends credibility?
What action is requested? Disclosure, login, payment, permissions, or another action?

sourceBody.text: This four-question approach is a teaching aid, not an official sequence of attack stages.
4. Why caller ID, voice, and personal details are insufficient
Caller ID is a displayed clue, not complete identity proof
Caller ID is the name or number displayed for an incoming call. Spoofing means making identifying information appear to come from a different source; here, the relevant example is caller-ID spoofing.

Caller ID can be manipulated. A bank or company number on the screen does not, by itself, establish that the person speaking represents that organization. [US Federal Trade Commission: Recognizing scams](https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-avoid-scam)
Distinguish the overall technique from one supporting mechanism:

items: Impersonation: posing as support staff or a manager.
Caller-ID spoofing: manipulating the displayed name or number, one possible technical aid.

sourceBody.text: Someone can call from an ordinary unfamiliar number and verbally impersonate support. Impersonation therefore does not require caller-ID spoofing.
A familiar voice creates familiarity, not certainty

AI (artificial intelligence) voice cloning can generate audio resembling someone's voice. Official consumer guidance warns that a familiar voice can be imitated. [FTC: Voice cloning and emergency scams](https://consumer.ftc.gov/consumer-alerts/2023/03/scammers-use-ai-enhance-their-family-emergency-schemes)
Do not reverse that observation into “an odd voice proves an AI attack.” Connection quality can also distort audio. Conversely, natural, fluent speech does not establish safety.
The defensive goal is not to recognize every artificial voice by ear. It is to avoid making important operations depend only on voice.
Knowing your circumstances does not grant authority

Lin's name and project might appear publicly or might have come from other sources. Hearing those details does not establish where the information came from, who is speaking, or what they are allowed to request.

This is a reasoning boundary: knowing a fact is different from being entitled to make decisions about an account. You do not have to prove how background information was obtained before pausing a suspicious request.
5. What trust boundary needs protection?
The caller is not simply asking Lin to chat. The caller wants a code that could help complete an account operation.
Authentication establishes whether the person using a service controls the evidence required for the claimed identity. Authorization determines which actions that person may perform.
An everyday comparison: confirming that someone is an employee does not mean handing them every key in the building.
Even after verifying that a caller really is a colleague, ask: May this information be shared with them? Can they approve this payment? Have the required steps been completed?
Why a genuine login code does not authenticate the caller

An OTP (one-time password or verification code) is generally valid under limited conditions and helps verify an operation. It might genuinely come from the platform without making the person asking you to read it aloud genuine support.

In our fictional scenario, someone attempting a login elsewhere could cause the real platform to send a code to the account holder. If the account holder is deceived into sharing it, another person might complete that verification. This describes a risk, not an established incident outcome. Records are needed to determine whether it succeeded.

MFA (multi-factor authentication) uses different types of authentication factors, such as a password combined with a device in the user's possession. It strengthens protection, but different MFA methods do not provide identical phishing resistance.

NIST distinguishes manually entered OTP and similar authenticator outputs from phishing-resistant methods: manual entry does not bind the output to the specific authenticated session, allowing it to be relayed to the real service. A session here is the particular authenticated interaction or connection context. [NIST SP 800-63B-4: Phishing resistance](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html#phishres)
For now, remember:

items: Initiating an operation yourself through a trusted entry point is different from supplying a login code at an unexpected caller's request.
Do not give login codes, passwords, or recovery codes to an unverified caller.
A claim that something is “for security” does not justify disabling protection or approving authentication you did not initiate.
Phishing-resistant authentication protects the authentication step; it does not decide whether every payment or disclosure is appropriate. M09-06 will examine the broader controls.

sourceBody.text: 6. Analyze the complete Northstar case: identify risk, then verify
The table below analyzes a synthetic teaching scenario, not a real investigation.

rows: A text directs Lin to a new destination to resolve a login issue
An unverified message chooses the handling channel
Open the previously used official entry point independently
A caller claims to be support and knows the project
Familiar background is treated as identity proof
Verify through existing trusted contact information
The caller asks for the login code
Authentication capability is given to an unverified person
Stop sharing and involve the official support owner
The caller demands staying on the line and avoiding company support
Independent verification is being obstructed
End the suspicious interaction and use the established procedure

sourceBody.text: Urgency alone does not prove fraud; real incidents can be urgent. But urgency should not eliminate verification. A usable emergency process defines who verifies, who approves, and how the decision is recorded in advance. The person on the phone should not invent all the rules.
7. How can verification genuinely leave the caller's controlled chain?
Independent verification means using a trusted source that the suspicious request did not itself supply, control, or dictate to verify both the identity and the request.
Simply switching apps is not sufficient. A support chat opened from a suspicious text, followed by a call to the number that chat supplies, could still lead to the same operator.
For Northstar, Lin can:

items: 1. Pause: do not disclose information, approve a login, or install software.
2. Leave the suspicious interaction: end the call, without using the phone's one-tap callback option or contact details from the text.
3. Find an existing entry point independently: use the established company help desk, directory, or previously verified platform.
4. Verify the specific request: does the support ticket exist? Who requested it? What operation is needed? What is authorized?
5. Follow the approval process: if genuine, perform only the necessary authorized action. If unresolved, escalate to the responsible owner.

sourceBody.text: A support ticket is a work record with an identifier, description, and responsible person. Merely hearing a ticket number does not establish that the ticket exists or matches the request. Check it through the trusted entry point you obtained independently.

This procedure is a teaching design for the fictional organization. Official guidance similarly recommends a known trusted number or official website rather than a caller-provided number or direct callback. [Canadian Centre for Cyber Security: Verifying calls](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/what-voice-phishing-vishing-itsap00102)

If an established account itself may be compromised, asking that same account again is insufficient. High-risk actions should use another verified owner or independent approval under the organization's procedure, rather than relying entirely on one potentially compromised channel.
8. Organizations need more than “be careful”
This connects to M01-06's defense in depth: combine controls at several layers so one mistaken judgment does not produce the entire loss.
These are proposed controls for Northstar, not claims that every organization already has them.

rows: People and process
Established verification contact; permission to pause requests; simple reporting
Provide an actionable next step instead of depending on accent recognition
Accounts
Suitable phishing-resistant authentication; confirmation for sensitive operations
Strengthen authentication without declaring every business request trustworthy
Permissions
Only work-required privileges; different people confirm important changes
Limit the impact of one account or decision
Devices
Formal approval for installation and remote assistance
Prevent “help” from becoming unauthorized control
Detection and response
Login, permission-change, and ticket records; reporting and response procedures
Support discovery and investigation, while recognizing gaps in records

sourceBody.text: A legitimate remote-support tool is not necessarily malware. The key questions are who controls it, whether identity and authority were verified, and what operations are permitted.
Connections to earlier M01 lessons:

items: M01-01: CIA security goals. Confidentiality concerns unauthorized reading; integrity concerns improper changes to information or settings; availability concerns authorized users being able to use the service.
M01-02: Assets and risk. Accounts, materials, payments, and services need protection. Assess likelihood and consequences, not just how suspicious a message sounds.
M01-03: Authorization boundaries. This lesson analyzes fictional events. Actual calling exercises, evidence collection, and testing require explicit scope and authorization.

M01-04 and M01-05: Entry points and behavior. Calls, messages, and account-recovery workflows can become contact points. Analyze observed behavior rather than treating one warning sign as proof of a complete attack chain.
M01-07: Incident response. Control risk, then use records to establish impact, recover, and improve.

sourceBody.text: 9. Evidence: receiving a call, sharing a code, and account use are different events

Afterward, Lin says, “I answered, and I think I read out a code.” Security staff should accept the report, record what he did, and avoid blame. They should not immediately report that all company data was exposed.
The following is a teaching evidence matrix:

headers: What it does not establish by itself
rows: A text and incoming call appear on the phone
Corresponding message or call records exist
The displayed source is the real identity
Lin reports sharing a login code
Reported credential exposure requiring timely risk-based handling
A successful unauthorized login
The platform records successful authentication
That authentication transaction succeeded
The operator was an attacker or read all information
Unusual permission changes or downloads appear
Activity needs investigation
All changes were malicious or all downloads left authorized custody
An independent contact denies making the request
The claimed identity or request may have been impersonated
The entire origin and impact are known

sourceBody.text: Cross-check timestamps, accounts, devices, actions, tickets, and data-access records. A log is a system's recorded account of activity. It is an evidence source, not a guaranteed complete recording of everything that happened.

No unusual record does not guarantee safety: logging might have been absent, retention too short, or the relevant records not yet located. Conversely, an unfamiliar device or unusual time may have an innocent explanation. Investigate.

You need not wait for certainty before taking protective action, but your conclusions must stay within the evidence. If a password or login code was disclosed, or suspicious remote assistance was allowed, report promptly through the official channel. Responsible staff can protect accounts, handle sessions, and address devices as appropriate. Do not repeat suspicious actions to “check,” and do not erase all records yourself.
10. A two-minute tabletop exercise: trace where trust comes from
This is paper-based observation. It requires no internet access, accounts, or calls, and is not evidence of completed practical work.
Draw two paths:

visual.caption: Two verification paths
visual.description: Who supplied the contact details at each step?

items.title: Path A: the same source controls the chain
items.body: Path A: suspicious SMS → support link in the SMS → callback number supplied by that support chat → “Yes, that was us.”

items.title: Path B: return to an established trusted process
items.body: Path B: suspicious SMS → pause → independently open the established company help desk → verify ticket and owner → follow authorization.

sourceBody.text: At every step, circle who supplied the contact details.

Path A appears to check three times, but the suspicious source supplies the entire confirmation chain. Path B returns the decision to a previously established trusted process. That is the meaningful difference—not the number of apps used or how often someone was asked whether they really were support.
11. Common exam and real-world mistakes

rows: Vishing requires an AI-generated voice
Human speech, recordings, or other voice forms can be involved; AI is not required
Vishing, smishing, and impersonation are exclusive
Channel and technique can coexist; identify which dimension the question asks about
A text in a familiar conversation thread must be genuine
Display name, number, and thread placement cannot independently replace verification
No clicked link means no risk
A person might disclose information, read out a code, or follow verbal instructions
Confirming by phone is automatically independent
Check the source of the number; a number supplied by the suspicious message may stay inside the same chain
MFA makes phishing impossible
Authentication methods differ; secure login also does not establish legitimate payment authority
Receiving a fraudulent call proves compromise
Contact, exposure, login, action, and harm require separate evidence

sourceBody.text: Official guidance documents cases where spoofed messages appear alongside genuine SMS messages. This is a possibility, not a claim about every phone or every incident. [Canadian Centre for Cyber Security: SMS source spoofing](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/guidance/smishing-protect-yourself-sms-attacks-itsap00103)
12. One short check: explain in your own words

Scenario: An ordinary Northstar administrative employee receives an “account verification required” text. A caller then claims to be the IT help desk and correctly names a project. The caller requests a login code and says verification must be done by calling only the number in the text. The employee reports having read out the code. Platform login and data-access records are not yet available.
Use a few sentences to address this one scenario:

items: 1. If this is confirmed as an attack, which concepts describe the SMS, the call, and the claimed help-desk identity? Can they coexist?
2. How would you verify the request outside the caller's arranged channels?
3. Can you already conclude that the account was compromised and course materials were disclosed? Distinguish known risk, unverified outcomes, and immediate protective action.

sourceBody.text: No long response or confidence score is needed. Try your own answer before opening the reference explanations below. Reading an explanation is not a submitted learner answer or verified understanding.

sourceBody.summary: Reference explanation: 1. Can the three concepts coexist?
paragraphs: Yes. If a deceptive attack is confirmed, the SMS component is smishing, the voice-based inducement is vishing, and claiming to be the IT help desk is impersonation.

The first two mainly describe channels; the third describes a claimed identity. They are not mutually exclusive. Knowing the project name establishes only possession of that information, not a genuine IT identity. Evidence of tailoring to the employee could additionally support a targeted-phishing description, but the question does not require inventing a background-information collection process.

sourceBody.summary: Reference explanation: 2. How should the request be verified outside the arranged chain?
paragraphs: Pause disclosure, login approval, and software installation, then end the suspicious call. Do not use the number dictated in the text, and do not treat the displayed caller ID as a trusted directory.

Use the established company help desk, an existing directory, or a previously verified official entry point. Check whether the request, ticket, and responsible staff member exist, what operations are needed, and which approvals apply. An independent source matters more than merely switching to a phone or another app. A verified identity still needs authorization for the specific action.

sourceBody.summary: Reference explanation: 3. Can account compromise and data disclosure already be concluded?
paragraphs: Not yet, but timely, risk-appropriate protective action is warranted.

The available information includes receipt of the text and call and the employee's report of sharing a login code. This represents possible authentication-information exposure and should be reported promptly through the official channel. Protection should not wait for confirmed loss.

Open questions include what operation the code related to, whether it was valid, whether login or another verification completed, whether the operator was authorized, what subsequent actions occurred, and whether information was accessed or disclosed without authorization. Cross-check times, authentication and login records, account and permission changes, devices, tickets, and data activity.

The responsible owner can evaluate account protection, revocation of suspicious sessions, or device handling under the organization's procedures. Do not supply another code or reopen suspicious content for testing, and do not erase all evidence yourself.
In short: address known risk promptly; establish successful compromise and data disclosure with their own evidence.
Basis
[Canadian Centre for Cyber Security: Vishing](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/what-voice-phishing-vishing-itsap00102)
[Canadian Centre for Cyber Security: Smishing](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/guidance/smishing-protect-yourself-sms-attacks-itsap00103)
[NIST SP 800-63B-4: Phishing resistance](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html#phishres)
The explanation separates official terminology from reasoning about this fictional scenario; it does not represent a real incident.

sourceBody.text: Summary

items: Vishing describes the voice channel, smishing the SMS channel, and impersonation the claimed identity.
A familiar number, voice, background, or genuine verification code does not by itself establish a trustworthy caller or request.
Verify outside channels controlled by the suspicious source. Protective action can begin promptly; conclusions must follow evidence.

sourceBody.text: The next unit is M09-04: pretexting (constructing a deceptive situation), baiting (using an enticing lure), and tailgating (following someone into a restricted area). It extends these trust questions to fabricated situations and physical environments.
